request.prompt:
SCENE: Heart Chamber. The same hand and the same build as the reference image.

ONE single full-frame view. Not a grid, not panels, not insets. No text, no labels, no lettering anywhere, no interface.

NEAR VIEW. Inside the body: a close dark-red haze in the air, walls of flesh built from red, brown and pink terracotta and nether wart blocks, ribs and bone of bone blocks and calcite. 
A living chamber: dark sculk grown over bone like flesh, with faint cyan veins; sculk sensors and a sculk shrieker; a vast dark organic heart, a lumpy irregular mass of dark red flesh and bulging vessels grown into the wall (not a heart symbol, not a heart-shaped outline), with three round fleshy valves set in it; a young man in wet fisherman's clothes, Davey Coyle, stands by the heart, eyes open and far away; a very tall thin black figure stands in a corner facing the player.
THE LIGHT INSIDE THE BODY: natural light is part of the flesh surface — patches of glow lichen growing on the walls, cave vines with glowing berries hanging down from the vault, and many small soft points of light spread across the high vault like glowworms in a grotto; a few warm glows spill from lamps that are HIDDEN behind lips of bone and slabs, so the light shows but no lamp is visible. The lights are staggered and irregular in three dimensions — on the walls, on the vault overhead and low down — never a grid, never ore-like coloured specks, never glowing blocks laid over the flesh, never glowstone panels. The upper space is softly lit and readable, not black. Absolutely no cyan, teal or blue glowing blocks, no diamond-ore-like or sculk-catalyst-like speckled blocks anywhere on the walls or floor: the only light sources are glow lichen, hanging glow-berry vines, small warm points on the vault, and warm light spilling from behind bone ledges.
request.style_note: The Stranding: every image in this series is one place drawn in the same hand — a Minecraft Java Edition build shown as a high-quality in-game screenshot with a soft night shader. Every surface is made of visible one-metre cubic blocks with vanilla Minecraft textures (cobblestone, stone bricks, spruce and dark oak planks and logs, deepslate, mud and packed mud, black and grey concrete, prismarine, lanterns, glass panes), crisp block edges, no smooth curves anywhere: round or organic forms are stepped block shapes. The place is a grey slate-roofed fishing town on cliff terraces above a bay, a plain of wet black mud risen from the bay, and a vast stranded sea creature built of dark blocks lying at the far edge of the mud. Night under a clear sky and a bright full moon: cold blue-silver moonlight on wet mud and slate roofs, deep blue-black shadows, small warm yellow pools of lantern light at doors and windows, sea water near-black with silver moon glints. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, no text, no labels, no border, no interface.
